description: The version combination the OurFairy v1 backend is built and tested against. External dependencies (dsh, rikkahub) are pinned to exact product commits; the product repository itself locks its integration branch, because pinning a repository to its own branch tip would be self-referential and would fail after every merge. `researchUpstreamSha` is the upstream commit the readiness research was written against and is NEVER a product deliverable. A ticket worktree obtains the same combination by branching from each repo's `integrationBranch` tip and running scripts/combo.mjs verify.

ourfairy.note: Self repository: verify asserts the current worktree HEAD is the integration branch tip or an ancestor of it (the worktree is based on this combination), instead of comparing against a fixed commit. Product modules live under backend/, product launchers under scripts/.

dsh.note: Product commit currently equals the research upstream SHA: no product commit has landed on the fork yet. Native public-representation changes (owner/delivery/format) will advance productCommit while researchUpstreamSha stays fixed. build:lib:host builds the CLI/host libraries; build:native-system builds native/system/packages/linux-x64/bin/glibc/system.node, which the durable JSONL session writer requires (verified: without it a session flush fails to load the flock addon).

rikkahub.note: Baseline recorded for the Android client. First APK build is accepted by ticket #26; a missing Android build environment is not a backend blocker.

backend.agentModelNote: Single source of truth for the model selection this combination runs. The bundle's agent-default-model row declares the same pair for entry layers (ticket #28 consumes it); the launcher passes this pair to the probe, which passes it explicitly as agentOptions because no entry layer is mounted in the v1 baseline. 'doctor' checks backend/v1-bundle/cordis.patch.yml against these values so the two declarations cannot drift apart.
